questions.question: Fleming's right-hand rule can be used to determine the direction of induced current when the angle between the magnetic field and the motion of the conductor is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fleming's right-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of induced current in a conductor moving within a magnetic field.
 
• According to the rule, when the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the right hand are held perpendicular to each other:
 
 
• The thumb represents the direction of the motion of the conductor.
 
• The forefinger represents the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• The middle finger represents the direction of the induced current.
 
 
 
• Fleming's right-hand rule is most effective when the angle between the magnetic field and the motion of the conductor is **90º**.
 
• This is because, at 90º, the conductor cuts through the maximum number of magnetic field lines, inducing the maximum current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fleming's right-hand rule is different from Fleming's left-hand rule, which is used for electric motors to find the direction of force acting on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
 
• Michael Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction is the principle behind Fleming's right-hand rule.
 
• Faraday's law states that a change in magnetic field within a closed loop induces an electromotive force (EMF) in the conductor.
 
• Understanding these principles is crucial for applications in electrical engineering and physics, such as in the design of electric generators and transformers.

• The magnetic effect of electric current was discovered by** H.C. Oersted in 1820**__.
 
• He observed that the flow of electric current through a conductor produces a magnetic field around it.

 __

questions.question: What does the middle finger represent in Fleming's Left-Hand Rule?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

Fleming's Left-Hand Rule is a crucial principle in the field of electromagnetism, particularly in understanding the interaction between a magnetic field and an electric current. It is named after John Ambrose Fleming, an English electrical engineer and physicist who introduced this rule to predict the direction of force experienced by a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

**Fleming's Left-Hand Rule:** According to Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, if you align your thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of your left hand perpendicular to each other, each finger represents a different physical quantity:

 
• **Thumb:** Represents the direction of the force (or motion) experienced by the conductor.
 
• **Forefinger:** Represents the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• **Middle Finger:** Represents the direction of the current flowing through the conductor.

The correct answer to the given question is option 3: Direction of current. The middle finger in Fleming's Left-Hand Rule specifically indicates the direction of the current flowing through the conductor.

**Application**

Fleming's Left-Hand Rule is widely used in the design and analysis of various electromagnetic devices:

 
• **Electric Motors:** In electric motors, the interaction between the magnetic field and the current-carrying conductors generates a force that causes the rotor to turn. By using Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, engineers can predict the direction of the rotor's motion.
 
• **Generators:** In generators, mechanical energy is converted into electrical energy. Fleming's Left-Hand Rule helps in understanding the direction of the induced current when a conductor moves through a magnetic field.
 
• **Magnetic Levitation Systems:** In maglev trains, the principles of electromagnetism, including Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, are used to create lift and propulsion without physical contact.

questions.question: Fleming's Right-Hand Rule is applicable in the case of _________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**electric generators**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fleming's Right-Hand Rule** is used to determine the direction of induced current when a conductor moves in a magnetic field.
 
• This rule is specifically applicable to **electric generators**, which convert mechanical energy into electrical energy.
 
• According to the rule, if you stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the right hand such that they are mutually perpendicular:
 
 
• The thumb indicates the direction of the **motion** of the conductor.
 
• The forefinger points in the direction of the **magnetic field**.
 
• The middle finger gives the direction of the **induced current**.
 
 
 
• This rule is crucial in understanding the working principles of **electric generators** and is widely used in practical applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Motors**__

 __
 
• Electric motors work on **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule**, not the right-hand rule.
 
• This rule helps determine the direction of force experienced by a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, which is essential for the functioning of electric motors.
 
 
 
• **Fuse Wires**__
 __
 
• Fuse wires are safety devices used to prevent overloading in electrical circuits. They do not involve the application of Fleming's Right-Hand Rule.
 
 
 
• **Electric Kettles**__
 
 
• Electric kettles are appliances used for boiling water using electrical resistance. Fleming's Right-Hand Rule is not applicable in their operation.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about magnetic field at a point due to a current carrying straight conductor.

(a) It increases as the current in the conductor increases.

(b) It decreases as the distance of the point from the conductor increases.

(c) Its direction can be determined by Right-hand Thumb rule'.

Which of the statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All (a), (b) and (c)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The magnetic field around a current-carrying straight conductor increases as the current in the conductor increases.
 
• The magnetic field decreases as the distance from the conductor increases.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field can be determined using the Right-hand Thumb rule.
 
• According to the Right-hand Thumb rule, if you grip the conductor with your right hand with the thumb pointing in the direction of the current, the direction in which your fingers curl gives the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
• The magnetic field lines form concentric circles around the conductor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biot-Savart Law**

 
 
• This law helps in calculating the magnetic field produced by a segment of current-carrying conductor.
 
• It states that the magnetic field is directly proportional to the current and inversely proportional to the distance from the conductor.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field Lines**
 
 
• These are visual representations of the magnetic field around a conductor or magnet.
 
• They illustrate the direction and strength of the magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction**
 
 
• This is the process of generating electric current by changing the magnetic field around a conductor.
 
• It is the fundamental principle behind transformers and generators.

questions.question: The magnetic field outside a very tightly wound long solenoid is considered to be ___________.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Solenoid: A solenoid is a conducting wire wound into coils of many turns forming a cylindrical shape such that its diameter is less compared to its length.

 
 
• Each turn of the coil is treated as a closed circular loop, hence the magnetic field produced from it is considered as that produced by a circular current-carrying conductor.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66c63a320693aee608bfb76cdaeae8cbdefbe60ab7c33084913e066e5e5ff237.png] 

B={{{mu }₀}NI}

Where N = number of turns per unit length, l = current in the solenoid, and μo = absolute permeability of air or vacuum.

The field lines due to current in a circular loop are as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4515f230cbbfe4d0bad8a577b4f4a5ee29383990959fb93e3409826e2c2fd23f.png] 

 
• The net magnetic field in a solenoid is, therefore, equal to the vector sum of the magnetic field due to each loop.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• The magnetic field line is a straight line inside a solenoid. Hence, it remains uniform along its length.
 
• The magnetic field inside a solenoid is the sum of magnetic fields due to all loops. So, on increasing the number of loops, the number of electrons causing current increases. Thus magnetic field strength increases.
 
• The distance from the current-carrying conductor and the magnetic field are inversely proportional. Thus, towards the ends of the solenoid, the magnetic field strength reduces as they diverge.
 
• The magnetic field outside the solenoid is zero.

__
 
• Fleming's right-hand rule is used to determine the direction of induced current in a conductor moving in a magnetic field.
 
• Using Fleming's right-hand rule, if the direction of the magnetic field is towards north and the conductor is moving vertically upward, the current will flow towards the west.
 
• Fleming's right-hand rule states that if you extend the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of your right hand such that they are mutually perpendicular, with the thumb pointing in the direction of motion of the conductor, and the forefinger in the direction of the magnetic field, then the middle finger will point in the direction of the induced current.

• It is particularly useful in the context of generators and other devices where mechanical motion is converted into electrical energy.
 
• Conversely, Fleming's left-hand rule is used for electric motors where electrical energy is converted into mechanical motion.
 
• Both rules are fundamental principles in electromagnetism and are widely used in physics and engineering.

questions.question: The magnitudes of the magnetic field at a point at distance r from a straight conductor carrying current I, 2I and 3I, one by one, are B₁, B₂ and B₃, respectively. Which of the following relations is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **B3 > B2 > B1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **magnitude** of a magnetic field at a point at **distance r** from a straight conductor carrying **current 'I'** is:
 
• B = (u₀)/(2pi) (I)/(r)
 
• **As the magnitude of the magnetic field directly depends upon the current carried by the straight conductor.**
 
• Thus,** the higher the current** carried by the conductor,** the higher will be the magnitude** of the magnetic field at a point at distance r.

Thus, In the given problem, **B3>B2>B1, as the current is 3I>2I>I.**

• The** direction of force** on a current carrying conductor can be** changed **by changing the **direction of current **flowing through it.

• The magnetic field around a solenoid is** similar to that around a bar magnet**.
 
• The magnetic field lines move from south to north inside the solenoid and north to south outside the solenoid. Thus, forming closed loops. 
 
• Inside the solenoid, the magnetic **field lines move parallel to each other.** Thus, it is **uniform inside the solenoid. **
 
• The magnetic field is strongest inside the solenoid.

questions.question: Magnetic field lines at north pole of a magnet are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **lines emerging from the pole.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnetic field lines**

 
 
• **​**The **magnet or moving electric charges** create a field known as the magnetic field. The region within which the force of magnetism operates around a magnetic substance or **moving electric charge** is known as the magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/175de06bdbbf9738b8d7f0ca3ec60fb626e04dc1856f10ee60f1f51e2c9953fe.png] 
 
• Magnetic field lines are used to represent magnetic fields. It is a visual tool used to visualize the **magnetic field's direction and strength**.
 
• A **compass needle **can be used to draw lines in a magnetic field. Place the compass needle on a piece of paper close to the magnet.
 
• Mark the direction that the compass needle is pointing in after you have checked it.
 
• Mark the directions by moving the compass needle to **various positions.** The lines of the magnetic field can be seen by joining the points.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Properties of Magnetic Field Lines**

 
 
• The magnetic field's direction can be determined by** tangenting** the lines of the field.
 
• The **field strength **is directly proportional to the **density or closeness** of the field lines.
 
• Lines in the magnetic field appear to **start** at the **north pole** and merge or **end at** the **south pole.**
 
• The magnetic field lines that run** inside the magnet **run from the **south pole to the north pole**.
 
• Lines of the magnetic field **never cross each other.**
 
• A **closed loop** is formed by magnetic field lines.
 
• At any point on the field, field lines have **magnitude** as well as **direction**. Consequently, a vector is used to represent magnetic field lines.
 
• They indicate the magnetic field's direction.
 
• Because the field lines are **denser near the poles**, the magnetic field is **stronger at the poles**.

questions.question: Magnetic field lines never cross each other. This fact implies that the magnetic field always have ________.

options.text: double values at any point in space
triple values at any point in space
multiple values at any point in space
a unique value at any point in space

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a unique value at any point in space**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Why do magnetic field lines never cross each other?**

 
 
• **​**If magnetic field lines cross, there will be two directions of the same field at the point where they meet. This is not possible. So, the lines of the fields don't cross or intersect each other.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **What is a magnetic field?**

 
 
• The force of magnetism acts on the area around a magnetic material or a moving electric charge. This area is called the **magnetic field**.
 
• A magnetic field is made up of moving electric charges and the natural magnetic moments of elementary particles, which are linked to a basic quantum property called **spin**.
 
• **Magnetic field** and **electric field** are interconnected and constituents of the **electromagnetic force**, one of nature's four fundamental forces.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic field lines and their properties**
 
 
• **​**Magnetic field lines never intersect.
 
• The density of the field lines shows the field's strength.
 
• Magnetic field lines always arise from or begin at the north pole and end at the south pole.
 
• Always, magnetic field lines form closed loops.

questions.question: Magnetic fields produced by a current carrying conductor are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is concentric circles. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The direction of the magnetic field is perpendicular to the direction of the current flow.
 
• The strength of the magnetic field is directly proportional to the magnitude of the current flowing through the conductor.
 
• The magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor are concentric circles centered on the conductor.
 
• The magnetic field lines around a loop of current-carrying wire are similar to those around a straight conductor, but the lines are more tightly packed and the direction of the magnetic field inside the loop is opposite to that outside the loop.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64fa28bb78415971a58ec7852198fa965fb500573e020210d49e0cd04e5de48f.png]

• Magnetic field lines are not parallel to each other and do not have a semi-circular shape as they always form closed loops.
 
• Magnetic field lines do not intersect with each other as it would mean that the direction of the magnetic field at that point would be undefined.
 
• Magnetic field lines are those in a magnetic field whose density indicates the field's size and whose tangent at any given place indicates the field's direction.
 
 
• The quantity of magnetic field lines determines the strength of the magnetic field.

questions.question: If the magnetic field due to a single turn circular coil is B. Then the value of magnetic field due a circular coil with 10 turns will be: (Other parameters are to be kept same)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The magnetic field (B) created by a coil is directly proportional to the number of turns (N) in the coil.
 
• If a single-turn coil produces a magnetic field B, then a coil with 10 turns will produce a magnetic field proportional to 10 times the single-turn coil.
 
• The relationship can be expressed as B₁₀ ₜᵤᵣₙₛ = N * Bₛᵢₙgₗₑ ₜᵤᵣₙ, where N is the number of turns.
 
• Therefore, for 10 turns, the magnetic field B₁₀ ₜᵤᵣₙₛ = 10 * B.
 
• Hence, the magnetic field due to a circular coil with 10 turns will be 10 B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Field:**

 
 
• It is a vector field that describes the magnetic influence on moving electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials.
 
• The symbol for the magnetic field is B, and it is measured in teslas (T).
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction:**
 
 
• It is the production of an electromotive force (EMF) across an electrical conductor in a changing magnetic field.
 
• This principle is fundamental in the operation of transformers, inductors, and many types of electrical generators and motors.
 
 
 
• **Right-Hand Rule:**
 
 
• It is a mnemonic for understanding the direction of the magnetic field relative to the direction of the current.
 
• If you point your thumb in the direction of the current, the curl of your fingers shows the direction of the magnetic field loops.
 
 
 
• **Solenoid:**
 
 
• A solenoid is a coil wound into a tightly packed helix, which generates a magnetic field when an electric current passes through it.
 
• The magnetic field inside a solenoid is uniform and parallel to the axis of the solenoid.

questions.question: Which of the following gives the direction of the force acting on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?

**Fleming's left-hand rule**:

__
 
• **Stretch the thumb and the first two fingers** of the **left hand mutually perpendicular to each other**.
 
• If the **forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field**, the **central finger in the direction of the current**, then the **thumb gives the direction of the force on the charged particle**.

**Right-hand thumb rule**:

 
• When we take our **right-hand** and **stretch forefinger**, **middle finger,** and **thumb at right angles to each other**. 
 
• Then **the forefinger is along in the direction of the magnetic field**, the **thumb indicates the direction of motion or applied force**, then the **middle finger will show the direction of the induced current.**

**Maxwell's corkscrew rule**:

 
• If a **right-handed screw is rotated along the wire** so that it advances in the **direction of the current**, then the **direction in which the thumb rotates** gives the **direction of the magnetic field**.

**EXPLANATION__:**

Fleming's left-hand rule:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97816b0a4e50b2cf8836805733587a7545653103d525fd92a3901a48a0b5c394.png] 

 
• Stretch the thumb and the first two fingers of the left hand mutually perpendicular to each other.
 
• If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field, the central finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb gives the direction of the force on the charged particle.

questions.question: The magnetic field due to a circular coil carrying six turns will be _______ equal to the magnetic field due to a single circular loop carrying the same current.
questions.solution:
सही उत्तर '6 गुना' है।

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The magnetic field produced at a given point by a current carrying wire is directly dependent on the current passing through it.
 
• Therefore, if there is a circular coil with n turns, the field produced is n times larger than the field produced by a single turn.
 
• Thus, in a circular coil having 6 turns, the field generated is 6 times.

questions.question: The magnitude of the magnetic field due to a current-carrying circular coil varies with the number of turns n as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'__n__'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The magnetic field produced by a current-carrying wire at a given point depends directly on the current passing through it.** **Therefore,
 
• if there is **a circular coil having n turns**, the **field produced is n times** as large as that produced by a single turn.
 
• This is because the **current in each circular turn has the same direction**, and the field due to each turn then just adds up.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic induction(EMI):**

 
 
• Electromagnetic or magnetic induction is the production of an electromotive force across an electrical conductor in a changing magnetic field.
 
• **Michael Faraday** is generally credited with the** discovery of induction in 1831**, and James Clerk Maxwell mathematically described it as Faraday's law of induction.
 
• EMI is a current produced because of voltage production (electromotive force) **due to a changing magnetic field**.
 
• This either happens when a conductor is placed in a moving magnetic field (when using an AC power source) or when a conductor is constantly moving in a stationary magnetic field.

questions.question: Which among the following device is used to detect the flow of current in a circuit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Moving Coil Galvanometer**__.

__
 
• A** moving coil galvanometer** is an **electromagnetic device** that is used to detect the** flow of current in a circuit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• It is also known as the **Weston galvanometer**.
 
• It works on the principle that when a **current-carrying loop is placed** in an external magnetic field,** it experiences a torque**.
 
• The value of **torque can be changed **by changing the **current in the loop.**
 
• The **moving coil galvanometer** is made up of a rectangular coil that has many turns and is usually made of fine **copper wire** that is wounded on a metallic frame.
 
• **Deflection in Galvanometer** is directly proportional to current.
 
• Thus, the** scale of the Galvanometer is linear**.

questions.question: An emf is induced whenever there is a change in the magnetic field linked with electric circuits. This is stated by the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Faraday's law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction** states that an electromotive force (emf) is induced in a conductor when there is a change in the magnetic field around it.
 
• It is one of the fundamental principles of electromagnetism and is essential in the functioning of electrical generators, transformers, and inductors.
 
• Faraday's Law is mathematically expressed as **emf = -dΦB/dt**, where ΦB represents the magnetic flux.
 
• This law was formulated by **Michael Faraday** in 1831 through a series of experiments.
 
• It also explains the working principle behind inductive charging and various electromagnetic devices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Flux (ΦB)**

 
 
• Magnetic flux refers to the total magnetic field passing through a given area.
 
• It is measured in webers (Wb) and is calculated as the product of the magnetic field and the perpendicular area it penetrates.
 
• Magnetic flux is a key concept in understanding electromagnetic induction.
 
 
 
• **Electromotive Force (emf)**
 
 
• Emf is the voltage generated by an energy source such as a battery or through electromagnetic induction.
 
• It is measured in volts and is responsible for driving the current through a circuit.
 
 
 
• **Lenz's Law**
 
 
• Lenz's Law states that the direction of the induced emf and current will oppose the change in magnetic flux that caused them.
 
• This law ensures conservation of energy and is essential in determining the direction of induced currents.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Faraday's Law**
 
 
• Faraday's Law is used in the design and operation of electric generators, transformers, and inductors.
 
• It is also applied in various technologies such as magnetic flow meters and inductive charging systems.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about a magnetic field.

(i) A magnetic field has both magnitude and direction.

(ii) Magnetic field lines due to a bar magnet originate from its north pole and terminate at its south pole.

(iii) The relative strength of a magnetic field is shown by the degree of closeness of the field lines.

Select the correct option.
questions.solution:
__Concept__:

Magnetic field:

__
 
• The area around a magnet where a magnetic force is experienced is called the magnetic field.
 
• It is a quantity that has both direction and magnitude,__ (i.e., Vector quantity).

__Explanation__:

__
 
• A magnetic field has both magnitude and direction:
 
 
• Reason: It is a vector quantity. 
 
 
 
• The direction of magnetic field lines inside a bar magnet is from its south pole to its north pole.
 
• Magnetic field lines are closed curves. 
 
• Outside the magnet**, the direction of the magnetic field line is taken from the North pole to the South Pole.**__
 
• Inside the magnet, the direction of the magnetic field line is taken from the South pole to the North pole.
 
• Therefore, magnetic field lines are closed curves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/175de06bdbbf9738b8d7f0ca3ec60fb626e04dc1856f10ee60f1f51e2c9953fe.png] ​

(i) A magnetic field has both magnitude and direction. - __**Correct**__

(ii) Magnetic field lines due to a bar magnet originate from its north pole and terminate at its south pole. -__** Correct**__

(iii) The relative strength of a magnetic field is shown by the degree of closeness of the field lines. -__** Correct**__
